Rashi on Chullin 16b:10:1.hebrew: בסימונא דאגמא - עשב הגדל באגמי מים, וקרי לישק"א, וכשהוא יבש חדוד וחותך, ואין קיסמין נבדלים הימנו:
Rashi on Chullin 16b:10:1.english: With the simona of the marsh - A plant that grows in water marshes, and is called in the vernacular "lishka," and when it is dry it is sharp and cuts, and no splinters break off from it.

Rashi on Chullin 16b:11:1.hebrew: דזיגי - צלולים, ואם יכנס בהם קיסם נראה:
Rashi on Chullin 16b:11:1.english: Glass [vessels] - They are clear, and if a splinter gets into them it is visible.

Rashi on Chullin 16b:11:2.hebrew: זיג - קלי"ר בלע"ז, כעין מראה שקורין מירדויי"ר:
Rashi on Chullin 16b:11:2.english: Zig - [Called] "clier" in the vernacular [Old French] - similar to a mirror, which is called "mirdoyir" [i.e., a mirror].

Rashi on Chullin 16b:11:3.hebrew: דרכיך - ואין צריך לדוחקו בחתיכתו, ואין קסמין נבדלין:
Rashi on Chullin 16b:11:3.english: That is soft - [Rav Pappa would cut only soft meat with the knife stuck in the wall] since there is no need to press it while cutting it, and no wood chips become detached [from the wall].

Rashi on Chullin 16b:12:1.hebrew: שיניו נושרות - שיני הפרק ושיני הכרכשא, שהיא מחוברת בהן לעצמותיהן, כעין תלתולי בשר:
Rashi on Chullin 16b:12:1.english: His teeth fall out - [This refers to] the teeth of the [anal] joint and the teeth of the rectum, which is attached by these to their bones, like fleshy protuberances.

Rashi on Chullin 16b:13:1.hebrew: הכל בשחיטה - והכי משמע: את הכל צריך לשחוט, ואפילו עוף, ואע"ג דלא כתיב ביה שחיטה בהדיא:
Rashi on Chullin 16b:13:1.english: All [creatures require] slaughtering - This is what it means: everything must be slaughtered, even a bird, even though slaughtering is not explicitly written regarding it.

Rashi on Chullin 16b:14:1.hebrew: לעולם שוחטין - לעולם מותר לשחוט ולאכול:
Rashi on Chullin 16b:14:1.english: One may always slaughter - It is always permitted to slaughter and eat.

Rashi on Chullin 16b:14:2.hebrew: מאן תנא - דמתניתין, דאיצטריך ליה למימר דישראל מותרין לשחוט ולאכול, דהא תנא ליה רישא הכל שוחטין לאתויי כל הנך דאצטריכו לאתויי שראוין לשחוט, כגון כותי ומומר וטמא, בחולין:
Rashi on Chullin 16b:14:2.english: Who is the tanna - [This question is about the source that parallels] our mishna, which found it necessary to state that Israelites are permitted to slaughter and eat, since [the mishna] already taught in its first clause, "Everyone may slaughter," to include all those who needed to be included as fit to slaughter - such as a Samaritan, an apostate, and a ritually impure person - with regard to non-consecrated animals.

Rashi on Chullin 16b:14:3.english: To permit them meat for [ordinary] desire - When they would enter the land, they would be able to eat meat for their craving, without any sacrifice.

Rashi on Chullin 16b:15:1.english: That from the beginning - [Meaning] when they were in the wilderness, from when the Mishkan (Tabernacle) was erected.

Rashi on Chullin 16b:15:2.hebrew: נאסר להם בשר תאוה - שאין יכולין לאכול אלא בשר שלמים, ואם היו שוחטין בלא קרבן היו ענושים כרת, כדכתיב (ויקרא יז) ואל פתח אהל מועד לא הביאו וגו':
Rashi on Chullin 16b:15:2.english: Meat of desire was forbidden to them - For they could only eat the meat of peace-offerings, and if they slaughtered without [bringing] a sacrifice, they were punished with karet, as it is written (Leviticus 17) "and did not bring it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, etc."

Rashi on Chullin 16b:15:3.english: They entered the land - They became distant from the altar.

Rashi on Chullin 16b:15:4.english: It was permitted to them - From this verse, that they may slaughter meat for their craving and eat it.

Rashi on Chullin 16b:16:1.hebrew: ועכשיו שגלו כו' - לאו רבי ישמעאל קאמר ליה, אלא רבה קאמר ליה לאוקמי דמתניתין דרבי ישמעאל היא, כלומר: ולהכי תנא לעולם שוחטין, דלא תימא עכשיו שגלו יחזרו לאיסורן כמו שהיו קודם שנכנסו לארץ, לכך שנינו כו':
Rashi on Chullin 16b:16:1.english: And now that they were exiled, etc. - It is not Rabbi Yishmael who says this; rather, it is Rabbah who says it, in order to establish that the mishna is in accordance with Rabbi Yishmael. That is to say: this is why it taught "We always slaughter" - lest you say that now that they were exiled, they would revert to their prohibition as it was before they entered the Land; therefore we learned, etc.

Rashi on Chullin 16b:17:1.hebrew: לעולם שוחטין ואוכלין מבעי ליה - כיון דלאו להלכות שחיטה אתי לאורויי, אלא להתיר אכילת בשר חוצה לארץ, ליתני לעולם שוחטין ואוכלין, והיכי שבק לעיקר מילתא ונקט שחיטה לחודה? ומדשבק לאכילה, ש"מ לא איצטריך לאורויי לן אלא מידי דשחיטה. ועוד, למה ליה לאשמועינן הא? וכי מהיכן תיסק אדעתין למימר יחזרו לאיסורן הראשון:
Rashi on Chullin 16b:17:1.english: It should have said, "One may always slaughter and eat" - Since [the mishna] did not come to teach the laws of slaughter, but rather to permit the eating of meat outside the Land [of Israel], it should have taught, "One may always slaughter and eat." And how could it omit the main point and mention only slaughtering? And since it omitted eating, this shows that it only needed to teach us something about slaughter. Furthermore, why did it need to teach us this at all? For from where would it ever occur to us to say that they would revert to their original prohibition?

Rashi on Chullin 16b:17:2.english: Originally - [This refers to the time] in the wilderness.

Rashi on Chullin 16b:17:3.hebrew: מאי טעמא איתסר משום דהוי מיקרבי למשכן - והיו יכולין להקריב קרבנות מכל בשר תאותן, ויקריבו הדם והחלב לבדו ואוכלין הבשר, ולבסוף כשנכנסו לארץ והיתה ארצם רחבה, והרחוקים לא היו יכולים לבא בירושלים בכל יום:
Rashi on Chullin 16b:17:3.english: What is the reason it was forbidden? Because they were close to the Tabernacle - They were able to bring sacrifices from all the meat they craved, offering only the blood and fat and eating the [rest of the] meat. But ultimately, when they entered the land and their territory became spread out, those who lived far away were not able to come to Jerusalem every day.

Rashi on Chullin 16b:1:1.english: What is [the law] regarding slaughter? - Rava could not infer [the answer] from that [case] mentioned above, as he goes on to explain.

Rashi on Chullin 16b:5:1.hebrew: תא שמע במחובר לקרקע כו' - ואוקימנא לעיל בתלוש ולבסוף חברו:
Rashi on Chullin 16b:5:1.english: Come and hear: In the case of something attached to the ground, etc. - And we established above that [this Baraita is discussing] something detached and then reattached.

Rashi on Chullin 16b:5:2.hebrew: דלמא פרושי קא מפרש לה - בסיפא, מאי מחובר לקרקע דאמינא לך כשרה? כגון נעץ סכין בכותל, דלאו חבור הוא, דודאי לא מבטל ליה התם, דהא גבי הדדי קתני להו לעיל: ונעץ סכין בכותל, סיפא דההוא דמחובר לקרקע הוא, ואיכא למימר דפירושא דרישא הוא:
Rashi on Chullin 16b:5:2.english: Perhaps it is merely explaining it - [The Gemara continues:] In what follows, what is [the case of] "attached to the ground" that I would tell you is valid? Such as one who stuck a knife into a wall, which is not [true] attachment, for he certainly does not nullify its [status as a vessel] there. For behold, these two [cases] are taught together above: "...and one who stuck a knife into a wall" is the last clause of that [teaching], which refers to "attached to the ground"; and one can say that it is an explanation of the first clause.

Rashi on Chullin 16b:6:1.hebrew: לא שנו - דנעץ סכין בכותל, כשרה:
Rashi on Chullin 16b:6:1.english: They only taught this - [in the case] where he stuck the knife into the wall, that it is valid:

Rashi on Chullin 16b:6:2.english: Rather, the knife is above - Its edge faces the ground.

Rashi on Chullin 16b:6:3.english: And the animal's neck below - [Meaning:] he moves the animal's neck back and forth [against the knife].

Rashi on Chullin 16b:6:4.english: We are concerned lest he press [the knife in, rather than drawing it back and forth] - Since the neck bears down heavily upon the knife.

Rashi on Chullin 16b:7:1.english: But it was taught - Above (Chullin 15b), regarding [an item] attached [to the ground]: "Whether the knife is above..." etc.

Rashi on Chullin 16b:8:1.hebrew: לצדדין קתני - דהא רישא דברייתא תנא תלוש ומחובר, כדקתני בכל שוחטין בין בתלוש בין במחובר, וכי הדר וסיים סיפא בין שהסכין למעלה כו', לאו תרווייהו אתלוש ותרווייהו אמחובר קיימי, אלא חדא אתלוש וחדא אמחובר:
Rashi on Chullin 16b:8:1.english: It teaches disjunctively - For the first clause of the baraita taught both detached and attached, as it taught: "One may slaughter with anything, whether with something detached or attached." And when it then goes on and concludes the latter clause, "whether the knife is above...," etc., it is not that both [clauses] refer to detached and both refer to attached; rather, one refers to detached and the other refers to attached.

Rashi on Chullin 16b:8:2.hebrew: סכין למטה וצואר בהמה למעלה אתלוש - דאדם אוחז בסכין למטה ושוחט, והבהמה תלויה באויר, וזה מוליך ומביא הסכין. והא דקתני סכין למעלה וצואר בהמה למטה - אמחובר, כלומר אף אמחובר:
Rashi on Chullin 16b:8:2.english: "The knife below and the animal's neck above" refers to [the case of] "detached" - For a person holds the knife below and slaughters, and the animal hangs in the air, and he moves the knife back and forth. And that which it taught "the knife above and the animal's neck below" - [that] refers to [the case of] "attached," meaning, [the same applies] even to [the case of] "attached."

Rashi on Chullin 16b:8:3.hebrew: רב פפא אמר - לא תוקמא בשינויא דחיקא, אלא תרווייהו אתלוש ואמחובר קיימי, ואפילו הכי לא תקשי לרב ענן, דהא דקתני סכין למטה וצואר למעלה במחובר - בעופא דקליל, ובהמה דקתני לאו דוקא:
Rashi on Chullin 16b:8:3.english: Rav Pappa said - Do not establish [the baraita] by means of a forced distinction [like Rav Zevid's]; rather, both [cases] - knife below and neck above, and knife above and neck below - hold true for both a detached and an attached [knife]. And even so, this does not pose a difficulty for Rav Anan, for when it teaches that the knife below and the neck above [is valid] with an attached [knife], that is [referring] to a bird, which is light; and when it teaches [this about] an animal, it is not exact.

Rashi on Chullin 16b:9:1.hebrew: ה' דברים כו' - כולהו משום שכשדוחקין אותם קיסמין ניתזין ומפרשים הימנה, ואיכא סכנתא במילה שלא תנקוב הגיד ומשוי ליה כרות שפכה, וגבי שחיטה דלמא מנקבא להו לסימנין, וכן לגבי קינוח דלמא מנקבא לכרכשיה:
Rashi on Chullin 16b:9:1.english: Five things, etc. - All of them are for the same reason: since when one presses them, splinters fly off and split away from it. And there is a danger in circumcision that it might puncture the membrum and render him one whose member is severed; and regarding slaughter, lest it puncture the simanim; and likewise regarding wiping [oneself], lest it puncture his intestines.

Tosafot on Chullin 16b:14:1.hebrew: שבתחלה נאסר להם בשר תאוה - פירש בקונטרס מדכתיב (ויקרא יז) אשר ישחט מחוץ למחנה ואל פתח אהל מועד לא הביאו, וקשה, דההוא קרא לא איירי אלא בקדשים ובשחוטי חוץ. ולקמן נמי דקאמר אלא לרבי ישמעאל דאמר בשר תאוה איתסר להו, צבי ואיל גופייהו מי הוי שרי, הא פשיטא דההוא קרא לא איירי אלא בקרבן בהמה. ונראה לפרש, מדאיצטריך קרא להתיר להם בשר תאוה, דייק מכלל דמעיקרא אסור; ומהאי טעמא דייק נמי רבי עקיבא שבתחלה הותר להם בשר נחירה, מדאיצטריך קרא לאסור:
Tosafot on Chullin 16b:14:1.english: That initially, meat of desire (basar ta'avah) was forbidden to them - Rashi explained [this] from the fact that it is written (Leviticus 17), "who slaughters [an ox, sheep, or goat]... outside the camp and did not bring it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting." But this is difficult, for that verse deals only with consecrated offerings and with [offerings] slaughtered outside [the Temple court]. And further on too, where it says: rather, according to Rabbi Yishmael who holds that meat of desire was forbidden to them, were a gazelle and a deer themselves then permitted [without being brought to the Tent of Meeting]? This is obviously not so, for that verse deals only with an animal offering. It therefore seems [better] to explain that from the fact that a verse was needed to permit them meat of desire, one infers by implication that beforehand it was forbidden. And for this same reason Rabbi Akiva also infers that initially meat of nechirah (killed by stabbing rather than proper slaughter) was permitted to them, from the fact that a verse was needed to forbid it.

Tosafot on Chullin 16b:1:1.hebrew: תלוש ולבסוף חברו לענין שחיטה מאי - תימה, מאי קמיבעיא ליה? הא אסיקנא לעיל (חולין דף טו:) דלרבי דיעבד כשר, ולרבי חייא כשר נמי לכתחלה; ואי לא ידע הנהו ברייתות, מכל מקום על כרחך יש להוכיח ממתניתין דתלוש ולבסוף חברו בדיעבד כשר ולא לכתחלה, דאפילו מוקי מתניתין במחובר מעיקרו ואסור לכתחלה שמא ידרוס, ה"נ תלוש ולבסוף חברו יאסר לכתחלה מהאי טעמא. ויש לומר דאליבא דרבי מבעיא ליה, דדלמא הוי כתלוש וכשרה, כדאמרי' לעיל, או שמא לרבי אין חילוק בין תלוש ולבסוף חברו למחובר מעיקרו ופסולה, ומתניתין דמכשיר דיעבד כרבי חייא, ולכתחלה לא שמא ידרוס, וברייתא דמכשר לכתחלה בעופא דקליל, כדמשני לקמן, אע"ג דקתני בה בהמה, אי נמי כרב זביד דאמר לצדדין קתני: ובצואר בהמה למטה שרי לכתחלה אפילו במחובר מעיקרו, וכשצואר בהמה למעלה אסור לכתחלה שמא ידרוס, ובכל מחובר איירי; וקא בעי למיפשט מברייתא דהיה צור יוצא מן הכותל דשחיטתה פסולה, ע"כ רבי היא. אבל קשה, דהיכי מצי לאוקומי מתניתין כרבי חייא, הא פסול צפורן במחוברת במתניתין אפילו דיעבד? ואמאי דהוה בעי לאוקומי לעיל מתניתין כרבי חייא, לא קשיא, דלא קיימא מסקנא הכי:
Tosafot on Chullin 16b:1:1.english: Something detached and then attached, regarding slaughter, what [is the law]? - This is surprising: what is he asking? Haven't we already concluded above (Chullin 15b) that according to Rebbi it is kosher after the fact (bedieved), and according to Rebbi Chiyya it is kosher even ab initio (lechatchila)? And even if he did not know those beraitot, in any case one must necessarily prove from our Mishnah that "detached and then attached" is kosher bedieved but not lechatchila - for even if you establish the Mishnah as referring to something attached from the outset, and [say it is] forbidden lechatchila lest he press [the knife] (yidros), so too here, "detached and then attached" should be forbidden lechatchila for this same reason. And one can say that he is asking this according to Rebbi: perhaps it is considered like something detached and is kosher, as we said above; or perhaps according to Rebbi there is no difference between "detached and then attached" and "attached from the outset," and it is invalid. And the Mishnah, which validates it bedieved, is like Rebbi Chiyya, but not lechatchila, lest he press [the knife]; and the beraita which validates it lechatchila speaks of a bird, since it is light, as is resolved below, even though it teaches "behemah" (a large animal) in it - or alternatively, [this works out] like Rav Zevid, who says it is taught in respective clauses: when the animal's neck is on the bottom, it is permitted lechatchila even for something attached from the outset; and when the animal's neck is on top, it is forbidden lechatchila lest he press [the knife] - and this [latter clause] speaks entirely of something attached. And he seeks to resolve [the question] from the beraita, "there was a rock protruding from the wall...its slaughter is invalid" - this must be [following] Rebbi. But this is difficult: how can one establish the Mishnah like Rebbi Chiyya, when the Mishnah invalidates [slaughtering with] a fingernail [knife] while it is attached, even bedieved? And as for the fact that [the Gemara] wanted to establish the Mishnah above like Rebbi Chiyya - this is not difficult, for the conclusion does not remain that way.

Tosafot on Chullin 16b:6:1.hebrew: אמר שמואל לא שנו אלא שהסכין למעלה כו' - משמע דאפילו בכי האי גוונא לא מכשר אלא בדיעבד, דאברייתא דנעץ סכין קאי, ולא אההיא דבכל שוחטין בין בתלוש בין במחובר; ואם כן, בצואר בהמה למעלה וסכין למטה קא פסול אפילו בדיעבד. וקשה, דאם כן הוה ליה למימר "חיישינן שמא דרס", כיון דאתא לפסול דיעבד. ויש לומר דאפילו אמר "ברי לי שלא דרסתי" פסולה, שמא ידרוס פעם אחרת. וכהאי גוונא אמרינן גבי השוחט במגל קציר דרך הליכתה, בית הלל מכשירין; ואמר רבי יוחנן אף בית הלל לא הכשירו אלא לטהרה מידי נבלה, אבל באכילה אסורה, אף על גב דלא שחט אלא דרך הליכתה, דגזרינן זימנא אחריתי שמא יוליך ויביא:
Tosafot on Chullin 16b:6:1.english: Shmuel said: They only taught this where the knife is above, etc. - This implies that even in such a case, it is valid only after the fact (bedi'avad); for [Shmuel's statement] refers to the baraita of "he stuck a knife [in the wall]," and not to that [other baraita] of "one may slaughter with anything, whether detached or attached." If so, where the animal's neck is above and the knife is below, it is invalid even after the fact. And this is difficult: if so, it should have said "we suspect that perhaps he pressed [the knife]," since it comes to invalidate [only] after the fact. And one can say that even if he said "I am certain that I did not press," it is still invalid, lest he press it another time. And we say similarly regarding one who slaughters with a reaping sickle in the direction of its stroke: Beit Hillel validate it. And Rabbi Yochanan said: even Beit Hillel validated it only to exempt it from [the status of] a carcass (neveilah), but eating from it is forbidden - even though he slaughtered only in the direction of its stroke - because we decree on account of another time, lest he move it back and forth.
